articleTitle: A Real-Time Forest Fire Recognition Method Based on R-shufflenetv2
abstract: The recognition of early forest fires can reduce the resource loss caused by fire combustion. A real-time forest fire image recognition method based on r-shufflenetv2 network is proposed. R-shufflenetv2 is mainly composed of a series of r-shufflenetv2 units and is an improved version of the shufflenetv2 network. In order to improve the recognition accuracy, the shufflenetv2 unit is reconstructed by using the residual structure, which enhances the feature extraction ability of the network. The experimental results show that the r-shufflenetv2 network is a good fire recognition model. On the benchmark FLAME dataset, r-shufflenetv2 has higher fire recognition accuracy than the original shufflenetv2. In addition, r-shufflenetv2 also achieves real-time detection, and its recognition speed is about 31 FPS.

articleTitle: Image-enhanced YOLOv5 and Deep Sort Underwater Multi-moving Target Tracking Method
abstract: Underwater target tracking has a wide range of applications in the fields of fishery resources research, marine ecological environment exploration and AUV/ROV operating in the deep water. The target tracking method based on deep learning is applied to the underwater environment, the YOLOv5 detection algorithm is used as the detector to identify moving fish under the water and the Deep Sort tracking algorithm is combined to realize the target detection and tracking task. According to the characteristics of complex underwater light conditions and low target contrast, the collected underwater images are enhanced. The experimental results show that the tracking method has a higher accuracy in detecting fish targets, a better tracking effect and a higher real-time tracking performance than YOLOv3, it's dection accuracy can reach 96 %.

articleTitle: Time-delay system compensation and intermittent fault tolerance control based on adaptive sliding mode control
abstract: In order to reduce the influence of time-delay and sensor intermittent faults on the system, a fault-tolerant control method based on adaptive sliding mode is proposed to improve the stability of the inner loop controller. Simulation results verify the effectiveness of the proposed control scheme.

articleTitle: Remaining useful life prediction of bearings with two-stage LSTM
abstract: Bearings are one of the most important rotating machineries of the running parts of high-speed trains, whose failure will cause serious safety problems. Therefore, the prediction of their remaining useful life (RUL) is critical. Stochastic process models and machine learning methods are two commonly used approaches for RUL prediction. Stochastic models, although with high interpretability for degradation mechanism, such as the two-stage degradation features of bearing, show poor ability when the degradation data are polluted with noises from field using condition. On the other hand, machine learning methods, relying on big data and advanced optimization algorithm, can achieve high prediction accuracy. Combining the advantages of both approaches, the paper proposes a two-stage LSTM method that uses statistical feature trends for stage division and LSTM method for RUL prediction. Application on the bearings dataset verified that the two-stage LSTM method is not only more interpretable but also has higher prediction accuracy compared with the traditional LSTM method.

articleTitle: Optimization and Trajectory Tracking of Deep Stall Landing for a Variable Forward-swept Wing UAV
abstract: This paper presents a trajectory optimization and robust trajectory tracking of deep stall landing for a variable forward-swept wing unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV). Firstly, the longitudinal dynamics model of a variable forward-swept wing UAV is established, and the aerodynamic parameters in a wide-range angle of attack (AOA) are obtained using computational fluid dynamics (CFD). Then, considering multiple running and terminal constraints of UAV deep stall landing, Radau pseudo spectrum method is adopted to generate optimal landing trajectory. Furthermore, to cope with the nonlinear and uncertain aerodynamic parameter at high AOA, a robust trajectory tracking controller is designed via combining feedback linearization and extended state observer (ESO). Finally, nonlinear numerical simulation is conducted to verify the proposed method. The simulation results demonstrate that the control accuracy of the designed controller under various disturbances can meet the landing requirements.

articleTitle: State Prediction for Smart Grids under DoS Attack using State Correlations under optimized PMU deployment
abstract: The measurement data plays a vital role in the self-detection and control of the power grid system. Denial-of-service (DoS) attacks have shown significant potential in disrupting the availability of the measurement data. Leveraging forecasting measurement data technique to defend against DoS attacks have drawn increased scholarly interest. This paper combines the optimal PMU placement (OPP) with state forecasting techniques for defending against DoS attacks. With consideration of the cross-correlations of nodes and the configuration cost of PMU, optimized PMU placement is obtained. The measurements have strong cross-correlations under the optimal PMU configuration. The forecasting technique utilizes the cross-correlations of nodes to forecast states of the system equipment under DoS attacks. The proposed method runs on the IEEE 118-bus bed. The test results have been verified the effectiveness of the proposed method against DoS attacks.

articleTitle: Bipartite Consensus Control for Linear Multi-Agent Systems with Disturbance
abstract: This paper investigates bipartite consensus control for linear multi-agent systems (MASs) with externed disturbance. In particular, we firstly proposes a dynamical sliding-mode control (SMC) protocol to deal with external interference of the system. In addition, we introduce a distributed nominal control protocol that relies on information between agents and their neighbors to implement the bipartite consensus of MASs. Finally, a simulation example which illustrates the effectiveness of the designed protocol is reported.

articleTitle: The Improved YOLO-V5 Based Automatic Non-parking Overloading Detection Method
abstract: Overloading of vehicles would cause serious damage to national public property, and further, it would also pose a serious threat to the personal safety of citizens. How to detect the vehicle overloading is particularly important, which has attracted a great deal of attention. However, it exhibits two major drawbacks, that are low detection efficiency and the poor detection effect, in the existing overloading detection methods, and thus the losses caused by the vehicle overloading cannot be effectively avoided. To improve both the detection efficiency and effect, in this paper we propose an automatic overloading detection method without parking, in which the computer vision technology and improved YOLO-V5 real-time detection algorithm have been utilized. To the authors best knowledge, there have not been reported works that explicitly address non-parking overloading detection. Three major steps are employed, leading to a high accuracy detection method. Firstly, the images collected in the actual road conditions are selected as the source of the data set. Secondly, in terms of the evaluation criteria, the model is trained for many times and the parameters are adjusted by the authors. Finally, the optimal parameters are obtained, which greatly improves the efficiency and effect of the detection. The test results in actual road conditions show that the method proposed in this paper has a high recognition rate and a fast recognition speed, which can greatly meet the actual application requirements.

articleTitle: An Improved Self-adapting Corner Detection Algorithm for Low-contrast Images
abstract: In order to suppress the impact of image dithering caused by wind-induced vibration, the features of sequential frame should be extracted. The Harris corner detection algorithm has been widely used for feature extraction. In the field of security monitoring and control, the image and video usually have the characteristics of jumbo size, high pixel and low contrast, which are difficult to obtain the corners. For the problems above, an improved self-adapting conner detection algorithm is proposed in this paper. Firstly, some of the corners are selected according to the comparison results between target pixel and the pixels around. Secondly, the selected corners are classified by reference to adaptive threshold values. Finally, false and marginal corners can be reduced or eliminated so as to select the best-matching corners. The above improved algorithm is validated in the field of sea area security monitoring and control. Simulation results show the effectiveness and feasibility of the algorithm above.

articleTitle: A Multi-missile Cooperative Guidance Law for Scattered Targets
abstract: A cooperative guidance law for multiple missiles with scattered targets is proposed in this paper. The guidance law is a biased proportional guidance law based on the double-integrator model by feedback linearization, and it is a kind of distributed cooperative guidance law which can achieve the purpose of each missile reaching its target point simultaneously in the two-dimensional plane ultimately. The numerical simulations prove the validity of the cooperative guidance law in this paper. The guidance law shows the unique characteristic of attacking multiple target points simultaneously, which is the feature that PNG does not have.

articleTitle: Improving Walking Assist Hip Exoskeleton Torque Efficiency with Decoupling Mechanism
abstract: Walking assist hip exoskeleton can aid healthy subject walking and reduce metabolic cost by providing assistance torque through both thigh bandages. Most hip exoskeleton thigh bandages are designed with direct and rigid fixation on the exoskeleton thigh links, leading to external forces/torques since the human and exoskeleton hip flexion/extension joints alignment cannot be ensured ideally. The external forces/torques reduce the walking assist hip exoskeleton torque efficiency. This paper presents design of a thigh bandage decoupling mechanism that eliminates human-exoskeleton thigh displacement deviation during walking. Human walking tests are conducted, and both thigh bandage and exoskeleton thigh link displacement during walking are measured through motion capture system. The interaction forces on the thigh bandage side are also measured by the force sensor. The results show effective tangential interaction force reduction with thigh bandage decoupling mechanism versus traditional direct and rigid fixation. Thus, the walking assist hip exoskeleton torque efficiency is improved. Meanwhile, the wearing comfort increases since external interaction force and torque are eliminated, which is proved by the subject's feedback after walking tests. The decoupling mechanism provides simple and effective solutions to higher walking assist hip exoskeleton torque-weight ratio since the torque efficiency is increased.

articleTitle: Lagrangian stability of memristor-based neural networks with unbounded time- varying delays
abstract: This paper focuses on exponential Lagrangian sta-bility for the memristor-based neural networks with unbounded time-varying delays. This paper utilizes the method based on the system solutions representation which without constructing Lyapunov-Krasovskii functionals to derive system stability criteria. A sufficient condition described by a few simple inequalities is guaranteed the exponential Lagrangian stability of system under consideration. Finally, the validity of the theoretical result is cearly demonstrated via a numerical example.

articleTitle: A New Polar Integrated Alignment Algorithm with the Aids of DVL and the Improved Polarized-light Navigation
abstract: The satellite navigation and the celestial navigation, as traditional auxiliary navigation sources cannot totally provide available and continuous information in the polar regions, especially under conditions such as magnetic storms and polar day. Consequently, it leads to the difficulties in the polar integrated alignment. In this paper, a new polar integrated alignment algorithm is proposed based on the azimuth and velocity, which are supplied by the improved polarized light (PL) navigation and the Doppler velocity log (DVL) respectively. Initially, the PL algorithm for the polar region is improved on the existing transverse navigation mechanism. Furthermore, the navigation coordinate systems of strap-down inertial navigation system (SINS), PL and DVL are unified. This paper builds the framework of the integrated alignment Algorithm of SINS/PL/DVL, and the simulation experiments are carried out. Eventually, the simulation results show that At 200s, the error of roll angle and pitch angle is less than 0.25’, and the azimuth accuracy is less than 0.8’, which means that the attitude errors of the integrated alignment system can be effectively estimated by the azimuth provided by the improved PL and the carries velocity provided by DVL.

articleTitle: Design of Differential Game Guidance Law for Dual Defense Aircrafts
abstract: A new type of differential game guidance law is proposed for the scenario of launching two defensive vehicles to intercept an attack vehicle in this article. First, according to the engagement scene, the relative motion equations of attack vehicle (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A$</tex>), defensive vehicle 1, 2 (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$D_{1}, D_{2}$</tex>), and target (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T$</tex>) are established and linearized around the collision triangle based on assumptions. Secondly, the corresponding cost functions are given and the pursuit-evasion problem is transformed into linear quadratic differential game problem. Finally, an analytical solution to this problem is obtained and the guidance law is designed by the differential game theory. The effectiveness of the developed guidance law is verified by nonlinear simulations.

articleTitle: Suppression of Moving Gimbal Effects of the AMB-rotor System Considering Multi-channel Coupling Current
abstract: The magnetically suspended control moment gyro-scope (MSCMG) can change the output moment by adjusting the angular rate of the gimbal. The displacement between the gyro rotor and the gyro room occurs when the angular rate changes, which is called moving gimbal effects, and it may lead to system instability if the displacement is large enough. In addition, the coupling of the multi-channel currents of the magnetic bearings brings new difficulty in suppressing moving gimbal effects. In order to suppress the moving gimbal effects, the process mechanism of the moving gimbal effects and the adjustment mechanism of the active magnetic bearing rotor (AMB-rotor) system are analyzed particularly. Then, the angular rate feedforward compensation method considering coupling of the multi-channel currents is proposed. Finally, the proposed method is validated on the MSCMG experimental platform, and the experimental results show that the moving gimbal displacement can be reduced by 66.1 % when the gimbal angular rate steps 15°/s.

articleTitle: Formation Tracking Stabilization Control for Fixed-wing UAVs with Planar Motion
abstract: This paper investigates the formation tracking stabilization problem for fixed-wing UAVs with planar motion under a directed graph. Assuming that the constant reference position and heading is only available to a subset of followers, a specified-time distributed estimator is designed to obtain the constant configuration of the leader for each follower. Utilizing the estimated desired configuration and defined formation shape, the saturated linear speed and angular speed inputs are designed, respectively. The novelty of this paper lies in the realization of the required pose formation tracking stabilization shape under the condition that the designed linear speed remains positive for all time. Finally, the feasibility of the designed formation tracking stabilization control law is illustrated by the numerical simulation.

articleTitle: Application of CenterNet Technology in the Process of Shipborne Aircraft Autonomous Landing
abstract: Shipboard aircraft autonomic landing is a very challenging task in the research of unmanned combat platform. In one image, the bounding boxes as an object in most successful object detectors, which is not only wasteful, inefficient, and requires additional postprocessing, but cannot meet the requirements of deck surface (small object) detection in large scene. In this paper, the CenterNet method, is simpler and faster than the object representation methods of past studies. The detector uses key point estimation to find deck surface center point and regresses to all other pose estimation parameters, such as depth, 3D sizes and orientation. CenterNet achieves the best results on our simulated deck surface dataset. And the same approach is used to estimation 3D bounding box of deck surface for point-based pose estimation. CenterNet is suitable for shipboard aircraft autonomic landing and runs in real-time.

articleTitle: Robust backstepping sliding mode control for coaxial tilt-rotor UAV
abstract: This paper investigates the problem of the modeling and robust control for a new coaxial tilt-rotor unmanned aerial vehicle (CTRUAV). The CTRUAV is composed of two pairs of coaxial tilted rotors at the front and one rotor at the tail. The dynamic model of CTRUAV is established on the basis of Newton-Euler formulas, and a robust adaptive backstepping sliding mode controller is proposed to realize the motion control of the CTRUAV under external disturbances. The controller includes two sub-controllers: an inner loop attitude controller based on adaptive backstepping sliding mode control and an outer loop position controller based on backstepping method, which guarantees that the closed-loop system is asymptotically stable. Finally, simulations are given to demonstrate the effectiveness of the designed controller.

articleTitle: Real-time Trajectory Optimization for Flexible wing-UAV Based on Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Flexible wing-UAV consists of a payload and a flexible canopy. It is widely used for the airdrop supply and aircraft recovery. However, combining the terrain constraint and control input management, it puts higher requirements on the real-time capability of the trajectory optimization. Thus, to improve the real-time capability, we present a novel trajectory optimization method based on deep deterministic policy gradient (DDPG). In this paper, a 3-degree of freedom (DOF) model is built by analyzing the data of the actual flight test. Then, the trajectory optimization methodology is designed based on the DDPG. Comparing with the traditional optimization method, the optimized trajectory of the proposed method does not need to be recalculated for the different initial values with the deep reinforcement learning method by building the optimization model previously. It shows large improvement on the real-time capability. Finally, the complete simulation results prove the feasibility and correctness of the proposed methodology.

articleTitle: Vehicle Load Monitoring Method Based on NBIOT
abstract: Vehicle load monitoring plays an important role in vehicle safety and vehicle scheduling optimization. In order to ensure the basic safety of vehicle operation and improve the level of traffic management, real-time monitoring of the load of transport vehicles is needed. In this paper, structural mechanics is used for vehicle load detection, and a monitoring method based on Narrow Band Internet of Things (NBIOT) is designed. Firstly, aiming at the problem of low accuracy of existing self-loading detection methods, a new detection method is proposed. The structural mechanics analysis of vehicle leaf spring is carried out, and the corresponding relationship between leaf spring deformation and vehicle load is obtained; Secondly, in order to suit the load conditions of different models, the radial basis function (RBF) neural network is used to calibrate the load on the cloud server, and in most cases, the fitting error is less than 0.6%; Finally, load monitoring is implemented through NBIOT and WeChat mini program. The load monitoring method proposed in this paper has the characteristics of simple sensor installation, no damage to the vehicle structure, good real-time performance, low application cost and wide coverage. The method plays an important role in further improving the level of intelligent traffic.

articleTitle: Spacecraft attitude tracking control based on MPC and fractional-order sliding mode control
abstract: Considering the problem of robust optimal finite-time attitude tracking for spacecraft, a unique characteristic of two advanced control methods, nonlinear fractional order sliding mode control (FOSMC) and linear model predictive control (MPC), combined in a two-layer controller was introduced. This method solved the global stability and robust attitude tracking problems of a group of reaction wheel-driven spacecraft in near-polar orbit under the action of unknown disturbances and uncertainties. The FOSMC controller guaranteed the robustness of the three-axis attitude tracking at suitable target points in the presence of disturbances and uncertainties. The two-layer controller part took into account the advantages of MPC technique to predict the attitude motive and constraints to provide the optimal target point required by the FOSMC controller. Finally, the reliability and superiority of the proposed method were verified by simulation results.

articleTitle: MPC-based Tilting and Forward Motion Control of Quadruped Robots
abstract: In many practical implementations, a quadruped robot needs to safely pass long and narrow space. This paper investigates the tilting and forward motion control problem for a quadruped robot to pass narrow space. We develop a model predictive control (MPC)-based control method for the tilting and forward motion control. In particular, we firstly establish a quadruped robot floating centrifugal motion model, based on which we design objective functions and constraints in MPC to generate command forces for robots' feet. In addition, we design the gaits and reference trajectory of the roll angle to achieve tilting switching and forward movement. The effectiveness of the designed MPC algorithm is verified via the simulation platform and hardware experiments. Finally, we discover the feasible range of roll angle maintaining stable tilting and forward movement via simulation experiments.

articleTitle: Anti-attack Fault-tolerant Control of Multi-agent Systems with Complicated Actuator Faults and Cyber Attacks
abstract: This study addresses the coordination issue of multi-agent systems under complicated actuator faults and cyber attacks. Distributed fault-tolerant design is developed with the estimated and output neighboring information in decentralized estimation observer. Criteria of reaching the exponential coordination of multi-agent systems with cyber attacks is obtained with average dwelling time and chattering bound method. Simulations validate the efficiency of the anti-attack fault-tolerant design.

articleTitle: Design of Attitude Measurement System Based on Multiple MEMS Sensors
abstract: In order to facilitate the students to obtain the vessel attitude information during the navigation internship in our school, this paper designed a system to measure the navigation attitude by using a combination of multiple MEMS. This paper focuses on the design of amplifying and filtering circuit, based on the selection of MEMS, then collect and process the output data, finally obtain the attitude information.

articleTitle: Deep Learning based Modeling and Control of Tiny Object on a Chladni Plate by Acoustic Vibration
abstract: Moving ting objects by acoustic vibration shows huge potential in precision medicine, chemical engineering and non-contacting precision control in the industrial. In this paper, we build a system for controlling the movement of tiny objects by acoustic vibration, and explored a novel modeling method based on Faster R-CNN. With the image recognition technology, the influence of the acoustic vibration can be observed clearly. Based on that, the simulation of moving the tiny objects is carried out. Then, by analyzing the simulation results, the feasibility and validity of the proposed method show huge improvement.

articleTitle: Adaptive dynamic task allocation and robust control scheme for target tracking
abstract: This paper proposes a dynamic task allocation and robust control scheme for the agents modelled as double-integrator systems. In the proposed approach, k-winners-take-all (k-WTA) strategy together with an adaptive finite-time dual neural network is used to realized the dynamic task allocation. The robust controller is developed based on disturbance compen-sation. The stability is proved in theory and numerical simulation illustrates the efficiency of the proposed scheme.

articleTitle: Adaptive Fault-Tolerant Control of Heterogeneous Multi-Agent Systems with Actuator Faults
abstract: In this paper, the time-varying formation control of heterogeneous multi-agent systems (HMASs) under a virtual leader is studied. The HMASs consist of an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) and multiple unmanned ground vehicles (UGVs). A fault-tolerant control mechanism based on adaptive technique and the radial basis function neural networks (RBFNNs) is proposed. In addition to the time-varying formation control of HMAS, the proposed control method can also accomplish the attitude control of the UAV. Finally, the effectiveness of the controllers is validated by simulation results.

articleTitle: Event-Triggered Anti-disturbance Tracking Control of non-Gaussian Stochastic Distribution Systems with Exogenous Disturbances
abstract: This paper presents an anti-disturbance PI control scheme for non-Gaussian stochastic systems subject to exogenous disturbances under an event-triggered mechanism. The objective is to control the output probability density function (PDF) of the system to track a given objective function. Firstly, the square root B-spline is commonly used as a tool for modelling the system output PDFs, and the PDF tracking control problem can be transformed into a finite dimensional dynamic vector tracking control problem. Secondly, the event-triggered mechanism is introduced into the control system, the disturbance observer based control (DOBC) method is used to estimate the unknown external disturbance and combine the state feedback to design a PI type dynamic tracking controller. Moreover, by designing the solution with a lower bound on the minimum trigger interval for event trigger greater than zero, it ensures that the Zeno phenomenon in the event-triggered mechanism can be avoided. Finally, The analysis of convex optimization theory guarantees the good system stability, target dynamic tracking and robustness of the stochastic distribution system. The effectiveness of the method is verified by simulating the styrene molecular weight distribution (MWD) model.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of TDLAS-based UAV Plume Tracing Algorithms
abstract: In this paper, we proposed a method that can be applied to solve the problem of plume tracing, in which a TDLAS gas sensor was installed on an unmanned rotorcraft to perform conical rotation scanning (CRS) to search for the plume, and compared with the Spiral-Surge algorithm. The TDLAS was installed on a three-axis aerial gimbal and it can maintain an angle to the vertical direction. While the drone is powered on and flying, by adjusting the yaw of the gimbal, the TDLAS continuously rotates and scans the three-dimensional space below the UAV. According to the time series of concentration line integrals of the odor detected in real-time during the flight, the UAV plans the path for finding the plume and tracing the plume, gradually approach the odor source and finally estimate its location. In the comparison on the CPTS-3D simulation platform, the detection direction of the TDLAS was a constant angle to the vertical direction in the CRS algorithm, whereas in the spiral-surge algorithm, the detection direction of TDLAS kept perpendicular to the ground. The simulation results show that, compared to the Spiral-Surge algorithm, the CRS algorithm proposed in this paper can find the plume in less time and has a higher success rate, and takes less average time to complete the whole odor source search process.

articleTitle: Observer-Based Load Frequency Control for Multi-Area Power System Considering Renewable Energy and Electric Vehicles
abstract: This paper studies the stability of multi-area systems with renewable energy and electric vehicles. First of all, the injection of renewable energy reduces the inertia of multi-area systems, by which the change rate of the system frequency deviation is accelerated. We use electric vehicles (EVs) to reduce frequency fluctuations. Since the system state is difficult to be monitored, we plan to use a observer to estimate state. At the same time, a multi-region power system dynamic model considering time delay is established. Using Lyapunov theory, the stability standard of multi-region renewable energy power system based on linear matrix inequality is proposed. Finally, the proposed method is verified to be effective by simulating the two-region power system in Simulink.

articleTitle: Short-Term Wind Direction Forecasting Based on Online Sequential Extreme Learning Machine
abstract: The stratospheric airship has received more and more attention in recent years because of its high social application value. In the research of the flight control of the stratospheric airship, the wind direction factor is an important factor that affects the airship's trajectory control. A large part of the power provided by the power system is used to overcome the influence of wind so short-term wind direction forecasting on the fixed-point position of the stratospheric airship is of strong practical significance. In this paper, we develop a short-term wind direction forecasting theory on the basis of Online Sequential Extreme Learning Machine(OS-ELM). Firstly, Mutual Information Method is adopted to calculate the delay time tau, False Nearest Neighbors is adopted to obtain the embedding dimension m. Then we reconstruct the phase space of the original wind direction time series. Finally, we use OS-ELM to forecast the wind direction data. The experiment results show that compared with other neural network algorithms, the OS-ELM algorithm has a certain improvement in forecasting accuracy and reduces the forecasting time, which indicates that the OS-ELM algorithm is effective in short-term wind direction forecasting.

articleTitle: Reliability Bounds of δ-Shock Model Under Non-Homogeneous Poisson Process
abstract: Some failure of the self-repair system is related to the interval of shocks. The delta-shock model can be used to describe failure mechanism related to interval time. In delta-shock model, failure occurs when the interval time exceeds interval time threshold. Traditional delta-shock models are mostly based on homogeneous Poisson process. This paper mainly derives integral expression of dynamic reliability under non-homogeneous Poisson process, and provides an equal-interval division method to obtain the upper and lower bounds of dynamic reliability. The influence of interval number and time interval threshold for the boundary range are discussed. The method is finally verified by a mathematical case.

articleTitle: L∞ fault estimation observer design for discrete-time linear parameter-varying systems
abstract: In this paper, an L∞ fault estimation observer design approach is proposed for linear parameter-varying systems. First, an augmented system is formulated with the aid of the state augmentation techniques. Then, the L∞ performance analysis is utilized to design the fault estimation observer and attenuate the influences of unknown disturbances, noises and fault variation. In particular, the presented observer has more design freedom and provides more accurate fault estimation results by introducing a novel observer structure. Finally, the feasibility and effectiveness of the presented observer are proven by a non-linear truck-trailer model.

articleTitle: Covariance Intersection Fusion Approach for Gait Estimation of Lower Limb Rehabilitation Exoskeleton Robot
abstract: This paper aims to study the gait estimation problem of lower limb rehabilitation exoskeleton robot, and proposes a gait estimation strategy based on covariance inter-section (CI) fusion. First, the discrete mathematical model of exoskeleton rehabilitation robot is obtained by Lagrange system discretization principle. Then, two groups of angle sensors with unavoidable measurement errors are employed to obtain the joint angles of the exoskeleton robot, and the gait of the robot is estimated by CI fusion filtering algorithm. Finally, simulation experiments show that CI fusion filtering algorithm can effectively overcome the interference of process noise, and greatly improve the accuracy of gait estimation during gait tracking.

articleTitle: Automatic Detection Algorithm of Mine Detection Based on Improved YOLOv5 in Complex Underwater Environment for AUV
abstract: In this paper, an autonomous real-time mine detection algorithm based on improved YOLOv5 in a complex underwater environment is proposed. The target recognition system based on the optical image is used to guide autonomous underwater vehicles (AUV) to achieve high precision mine exploration and assist the autonomous mine hunting weapon system to finish the mine-hunting task. In view of all kinds of various interference information of the underwater optical images, a set of image preprocessing systems has been added to the algorithm based on YOLOv5 which has the advantages of both detection accuracy and detection speed. The original data are processed by data enhancement, image enhancement, sample equalization, negative sample addition, and Poisson fusion, which can reduce the problem of poor detection results caused by the input image quality to some extent. At the same time, the number of layers of YOLOv5 is reduced, which makes the detection algorithm meet the requirements of the AUV embedded system without affecting the detection accuracy, and improves the real-time detection of the mobile terminals. The experimental results show that the proposed method could effectively improve the detection accuracy and real-time performance of the underwater mine detection system.

articleTitle: Visual Servoing of manipulator with moving base
abstract: Manipulator systems are necessary part for unmanned autonomous systems (UAS) to achieve task executions and hence, they have been widely adopted in mobile platforms, such as UAV, UGV together with visual feedback to perform different tasks. Due to the unknown movements of the base, it is difficult to achieve the accurate manipulator visual servoing control since the depth information is continuously changed. In order to achieve the manipulator visual servoing with moving base, two solutions are presented in this paper. Firstly, a support vector regression based method is developed to predict the horizontal movements of the base. Thus, the position of the end-effector can be adjusted accordingly so as to reduce the influence of moving base on the end-effector. Then, an observer is proposed to estimate the depth change in presence of disturbance acted on the camera velocity. With the estimated depth, a visual servoing controller is developed. Simulation and experimental results are presented to illustrate the performance of the proposed solutions.

articleTitle: Optimized Configuration of Electric Vehicles and Renewable Distributed Generation in V2G mode
abstract: Large-scale disorderly connection of electric vehicles (EVs) to the grid has significant impacts on the distribution network. Based on this background, this article aggregates large-scale EVs by time intervals, according to peak-valley price system and “Grid-Connected Reservation System” (GCRS), while the optimized configuration of renewable distributed generation (RDG) is taken into account. To achieve the goal of minimizing the active power loss of the distribution network, firstly, a mathematical model is established to optimize the active/reactive output of EV charging stations and the reactive output of RDGs. Secondly, a recently proposed Jaya algorithm is adopted to solve this mathematical model. Finally, an extended IEEE 33-node distribution network is provided for simulation, whose results show that, the optimized configuration of the EVs and RDGs can effectively decrease the load peak-valley difference, reduce the active power loss, and reduce the voltage deviation as well.

articleTitle: Composite Anti-Disturbance Control for Interval Type-2 Fuzzy System via Disturbance Observer
abstract: This paper concentrates on the matter of composite disturbance-observer-based control (DOBC) for nonlinear object provided with parameter uncertainties and the disturbance. The nonlinear system containing uncertainties is depicted by an interval type-2 (IT2) Takagi-Sugeno (T-S) fuzzy model. Based on the DOBC method, a disturbance observer is established to cancel out the disturbance produced by a single exogenous system. Then, the composite system is designed by combining the disturbance estimation with basic feedback control law, which can be promised to remain stable. Some stability results are acquired to ameliorate stability performance in the light of the Lyapunov theory. Finally, a numerical example is put forward to indicate the feasibility of the design theoretical method.

articleTitle: Maritime availability of BDS/GNSS ARAIM in the Arctic
abstract: High-integrity navigation as an essential prerequisite of activity is worthy of being investigated in the Arctic, which can be achieved based on Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS). The integrity performance of navigation in the arctic should be analyzed based on Beidou/GNSS in the arctic using Advanced Receiver Autonomous Integrity Monitoring (ARAIM) technology. Three different harbors in the Arctic were selected to simulate the changes of HPL under different combinations of constellation systems. The average distribution trend of HPL and availability at the polar region is also analyzed by using Stanford University's MASST software. The results show that the combination of two constellation systems can only meet the integrity requirements of ocean or coastal navigation. The availability of ARIAM is further improved using the combination of the three or four constellations, which can meet the high-integrity requirements of the ice navigation in the Arctic. In the case of BDS+Galileo+GLONASS and BDS+Galileo+GPS, the average HPL is 7.69m and 7.63m respectively. Using BDS+Galileo+GLONASS+GPS, its average HPL is 6.26m. All of them meet the requirement of HPL<10m.

articleTitle: Area Control of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles Swarm Based on Lanner-Jones Potential
abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) swarm area refers to the space occupied by a certain number of UAVs. By regulating the area of UAV swarm, the reflection area of radar is affected to reduce the exposure risk. To realize the effective modulation of UAV swarm area, inspired by the gas expansion phenomenon, an area modulation method of UAV swarm based on Lanner-Jones interatomic potential model is proposed. Firstly, the area measurement method based on the minimum convex hull algorithm is proposed to solve the bottleneck that the swarm distribution cannot be quantitatively analyzed. Secondly, on the basis of Vicsek flocking interaction model, the relative distance control method based on Lanner-Jones two-body interaction potential is proposed, which can realize the effective control of the global aera with the distance between two bodies as the unique variable. Finally, the simulation verification is carried out and the effects of the two control parameters named repulsion -distance and perception-distance on swarm aera is analyzed. The conclusion is that repulsion-distance is the dominant variable of swarm aera.

articleTitle: Continuous fixed-time sliding mode output feedback control for hypersonic vehicles
abstract: The fixed-time output tracking control (FTOFC) problem is investigated for a hypersonic vehicle(HV) in this article. Based on an input-output linearized model, a fixed-time extended state observer (FxTESO) is constructed to estimate the derivative and high-order derivatives of output tracking error and the external disturbances. Then, by using output tracking error and the estimations of its high-order derivatives, a continuous fixed-time sliding mode output feedback controller is constructed. The developed controller can guarantee system outputs converge to the reference signals in fixed-time. Finally, a simulation result is presented to demonstrate the effectiveness of the developed control scheme.

articleTitle: A dynamic neighborhood based multi-objective particle swarm optimizer for multimodal multi-objective problems
abstract: This paper presents a dynamic neighborhood based multi-objective particle swarm optimizer (DN-MOPSO) for solving multimodal multi-objective optimization problems. In DN-MOPSO, the whole evolutionary process is consisted of two parts. Firstly, the entire population is divided into multiple dynamic sub-swarms and the number of particles is randomly distributed in each sub-swarm. This is conducive to keeping population diversity and improving the speed of information diffusion among the population. Secondly, after the population is divided into multiple sub-swarms, there can be isolated particles that do not belong to any sub-swarm. By sorting the position information of isolated particles in space, we form a new sub-swarm of three nearby isolated particles to improve the convergence of obtained solutions. The comparison results between DN-MOPSO and other well-known algorithms on eight test problems suggest that DN-MOPSO demonstrates superior performance for solving different types of multimodal multi-objective functions.

articleTitle: A novel anti-swing initial alignment method based on polarization/geomagnetic fusion for ships working on unfamiliar waters
abstract: When the ship is sailing on an unfamiliar sea, the accurate initial alignment results attach much significance to the completion of navigation tasks. However, in unfamiliar offshore scenarios, the rocking and shaking of the ship caused by sea wind and waves cause great errors in the measurement data of gyroscope and acceleration in the initial alignment process, resulting in accuracy reduction or even failure of the traditional IMU-based alignment method. Aiming at this problem, this paper introduces absolute physical quantities solar vector and geomagnetic vector, and proposes an anti-swing rough initial alignment method based on polarization/geomagnetic information fusion. In addition, combing with inertial data, the fine alignment is carried out through the Kalman filter. Simulation results show that the ship alignment under swing conditions is achieved, and the alignment accuracy is significantly improved.

articleTitle: A Quasi Integral- Differential Type Event-Triggered MPC for Linear Systems
abstract: A quasi integral-differential (QID) type event-triggered model predictive control (ET-MPC) strategy for per-turbed LTI systems is developed. By considering the integral and the change rate of the error between the optimal prediction and its real state as the triggering condition, the calculation, and communication burden of the MPC method are significantly reduced. In addition, an improved robust constraint is used to handle additional disturbances. It is demonstrated that the QID ETMPC scheme is iteratively feasible and can stabilize the LTI system, and is further verified via a simulation experiment.

articleTitle: Automatic Optimization Method of Commutation for Position Sensorless Brushless DC Motor Based on DC-link Voltage
abstract: High-precision commutation is an important factor to ensure the high-efficiency operation and smooth torque performance of the brushless DC motor (BLDCM). In order to implement the position sensorless commutation, the commutation error is inevitably introduced from hardware and software implementation. To eliminate the commutation error, a automatic optimization method of commutation based on the DC-link voltage is proposed in this paper. First, the relationship between the commutation position and the voltage deviation of the DC-link voltage sampled before and after the commutation point is analyzed. Then, using the voltage deviation as the feedback quantity, a closed-loop controller is established to compensate the commutation point. Along with the voltage deviation converging to zero, a high-precision commutation is automatically reached. Therefore, the motor efficiency and output torque is optimized. Finally, the verification of the method is given by a magnetically suspended flywheel.

articleTitle: Automated tuning of MPC for VAV system based on LSTM
abstract: Model Predictive Control (MPC) is a mainstream control method, which has been widely used in the energy consumption system of modern intelligent building. The parameters of the model predictive controller significantly affect the response performance of the controlled system. However, in the existing technologies, most of the controller parameters are determined according to the empirical method to make the system achieve the desired response, which to some extent hinders the further promotion and application of model predictive control in the actual industry. Therefore, this paper proposes a MPC controller parameter tuning method based on Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) neural network. In this method, the overshoot, rise time and settling time of the system output are taken as the expected reference indices, and the controller parameters are tuned by LS TM to make the system reach the expected response. Finally, the feasibility of this method is verified in V A V system.

articleTitle: Design of Adaptive Sliding Mode Guidance Law Considering Trajectory Bulge
abstract: Focusing on the trajectory bulge problem of a high-speed missile with impact angle constraint, this paper designs an adaptive sliding mode guidance law with finite-time convergence based on the proportional guidance, and then derives an adaptive sliding mode approaching law which is suitable for fixed targets by constructing the Lyapunov function. A parameter adaptive intelligent algorithm based on the Actor-Critic network is designed in order to solve the trajectory bulge problem caused by the low correlation between the parameter of sliding mode guidance law and the missile flight state. Especially in the case of different initial trajectory dispersions, there are different degrees of trajectory bulge. The proposed algorithm takes the trajectory inclination angle error and the line-of-sight error as inputs of network, which can adjust the parameters in real time and effectively suppress the appearance of trajectory bulge. the effectiveness of the proposed guidance law is verified the simulation results. By compared with other adaptive sliding mode guidance laws, the proposed parameter adaptive algorithm can overcome the trajectory bulge caused by the initial trajectory dispersion, which then can significantly improve the terminal speed and enhance the robustness of the guidance law to the initial dispersion.

articleTitle: Research on HIL simulation with SIMATIC controller for Bladed
abstract: The stable operation of the wind turbine has a decisive impact on the power generation of the wind turbine, but the actual operating environment of the actual wind turbine is complex and the wind condition is uncertain. Therefore, the test control strategy needs to simulate the field conditions as much as possible. This paper studies the communication problem between Siemens controller and Blade simulation software, builds a hardware-in-the-loop platform for communication between SIMATIC427D controller and Bladed, and simulates the on-site environment of the fan to verify the effectiveness of the control strategy. Finally, through the experimental verification of the wind speed condition, the results show that the test platform can accurately verify the control strategy, and the platform can also realize the online modification of the control strategy, which greatly facilitates the research and development personnel to verify the effectiveness of the control strategy and improves the work efficiency, thereby improving the stability of the unit operation.

articleTitle: Unmanned Transportation System In Future Cities
abstract: In the future, the driving occupations of pilots and drivers will become the past. Unmanned cars, unmanned airliners, unmanned high-speed railways, and unmanned ships will be widely used. As the center of command and control of these unmanned transportation units, unmanned transportation system will play a more and more important role. The unmanned transportation system shall at least include decision control subsystem, equipment management subsystem, encrypted communication subsystem, intelligent life-saving subsystem, unmanned vehicle and other subsystems. In addition, unmanned transportation system as a new concept and new model also brings some notential risks.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of BDS/GNSS Single-Frequency Precise Point Positioning with Ionospheric Constraint in Polar Regions
abstract: BDS/GNSS single-frequency Precise Point Positioning (SFPPP) is a major mean to ensure the navigation capability of marine vehicles in polar regions. The sophisticated polar ionosphere significantly impacts the performance of SFPPP. In general, the ionosphere-estimated and ionosphere-weighted models are commonly used for processing the ionospheric delay in SFPPP application. The traditional ionosphere-weighted model sets the empirical constraint to the strength of the ionospheric constraint. The static and kinematic positioning accuracies can be several meters by applying inadequate empirical constraint in polar regions. An ionospheric constraint impact factor is constructed to determine the reasonable ionospheric constraint. Hence, the polar BDS/GNSS SFPPP considering the ionospheric constraint is proposed. The results reveal that the static and kinematic positioning accuracy of GPS, GLONASS, and Galileo are superior than 0.3 m and 1.0 m, respectively. Moreover, the static and kinematic positioning accuracy for BDS are superior than 0.9 m and 2.3 m. Reasonable ionospheric constraint can improves the positioning accuracy and fasten the convergence. The results of 32 high-latitude stations indicate that the static and kinematic positioning accuracy of the two models can reach 0.15 m and 0.5 m. The convergence time of the ionosphere-weighted and the ionosphere-estimated models can reach 3 min and 10 min, respectively. Multi-GNSS has superior positioning accuracy and faster SFPPP convergence.

articleTitle: Image Reconstruction with Event Cameras Based on Asynchronous Particle Filter
abstract: This paper proposes an asynchronous particle filter to reconstruct high dynamic range (HDR) video from low dynamic range (LDR) frame and event data. Event cameras have the characteristics of HDR and high temporal resolution, but at the same time they discard the absolute intensity information of the image. Traditional CMOS image sensors can provide low-frequency image with intensity information. In order to fuse the two kinds of information with different frequencies, we interpolate the image according to the inter-frame events. The HDR image is obtained by combining the two with an asynchronous particle filter (PF). For the any distribution of event noise parameters, PF is not limited by the event noise distribution and has a better estimation performance. By selecting some challenging scenes from the event camera datasets ACD and IJRR, the experimental results show that our algorithm can achieve higher quality image reconsruction.

articleTitle: A Resampling Strategy Based Adaptive Diagnosis Method for Industrial Machinery Faults
abstract: Currently, the fault diagnosis with balanced data and single-point characteristics has received mass concern, and the related research achievements are remarkable. However, because of the scarcity of fault signals and the correlation of faults characteristics, diagnosing mechanical faults ubiquitous in industrial systems remain a thorny task. Therefore, for finding a solution to the issue, a resampling scheme is developed, further, a diagnostic plan to industrial machinery faults is formulated in this paper. Firstly, a resampling plan is formed to get the balance diagnostic sample sets. Then, an improved cost-function is developed for enhancing feature learning richness of deep sparse autoencoder (DSAE). Next, a de-correlation condition is formed to weaken adverse effects of this correlation. Finally, necessary tests are carried out to show the excellent performance of the designed method.

articleTitle: Multi-spacecraft Cooperative Control Method for Malfunctioning Spacecraft Pursuit
abstract: The increasing number of satellites bring serious hazard for the on-orbit spacecraft. For the large malfunction satellites removal mission, multi-spacecraft cooperative pursuit and remove is an efficient approach. There are many constraints should be considered in the process of pursuit, including and no limit to, the collision constraints between service spacecraft, collision constraints between service spacecraft and target spacecraft, communication constraints between service spacecraft, and cooperative pursuit formation configuration constraints. It brings challenge to control the multiple satellites considered the multiple constraints at the same time in the process of formation reconfiguration and pursuit. For this problem, a novel cooperative control method based on task priority is proposed in this paper. Firstly, the dynamic equation of multi-spacecraft cooperative pursuit is developed. Secondly, the constraints of the failed spacecraft pursuit are analyzed, and the priority of each task is analyzed. The multi-spacecraft cooperative control approach based on the null-space behavior (NSB) method and the artificial potential function method are introduced. The advantage of the proposed method is that, it can avoid conflicts between the coordinated tasks, and meet the multiple constraints. In order to verify the proposed approach, a simulation of multiple satellites pursuit is provided, and the simulation results show the superiority and effectiveness of the method proposed.

articleTitle: A Novel Multiplicative Fault Observer for actuators of Satellite Attitude Control System
abstract: The actuator is an important part of the satellite attitude control system, and the damage degradation on it will have a serious impact on the overall control of the system. In previous studies, relevant researchers have made much effort in the additive fault estimation and the corresponding control design. However, the multiplicative fault estimation for the actuator still remains a challenge, especially when the fault is coupled with external disturbances. Therefore, this paper attempts to propose a novel sliding mode fault observer to estimate the multiplicative actuator fault coupled with external disturbances for actuators of the satellite attitude control system. In the designed fault observer, the super-twisting sliding mode algorithm is used to suppress external disturbances, so as to realize the relatively accurate estimation of the fault. A numerical simulation example on the satellite attitude control system is presented to verify the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed multiplicative fault observer.

articleTitle: Air Conditioning Cooling Load Prediction Based on LSTM-ANN
abstract: Cooling load prediction is the key to optimal control of air conditioning system, which is important for reducing building energy consumption. In this paper, a novel cooling load prediction scheme is constructed depend on a combination of long short-term memory networks (LSTM), artificial neural networks (ANN) and Markov chain. Firstly, the grey relation analysis is used to analyze and preprocess meteorological data and cooling load historical data. Then, the LSTM-ANN model to predict the cooling load is constructed and the ANN is optimized by beetle swarm optimization algorithm (BSO). Finally, the Markov chain model is applied to reduce the predicted error to obtain the final prediction results. The experimental results indicate that the proposed model has a better prediction performance than other existing models.

articleTitle: Polar SINS/USBL Integrated Navigation Algorithm Considering Acoustic Communication Delays
abstract: The integrated navigation system with an ultra-short baseline (USBL) acoustic positioning system effectively suppresses error divergence in the strap down inertial navigation system (SINS). However, the acoustic communication delay, and measurement outliers caused by the sophisticated polar underwater acoustic environment significantly challenge the SINS/USBL system. Hence, the Student's t-based delay Kalman filter (RstDKF) is proposed to relieve the influence of the acoustic communication delay and measurement outliers on the SINS/USBL system, and numerical simulations are conducted to verify its effectiveness. The results demonstrated that the proposed algorithm effectively suppresses the increasing position errors induced by the acoustic communication delay. Moreover, it also reveals that the proposed algorithm improves the positioning accuracies by 58.87%, 69.19%, and 87.20%, respectively, along transverse north-, transverse east- and up- directions, compared with the time delay Kalman filter considering measurement noise as Gaussian distribution.

articleTitle: Condition-based Maintenance Optimization of Multiple-Component Series System under Semi-Markov Analytical Framework
abstract: This paper provides an opportunistic condition-based maintenance strategy for a two-component industrial serial system subject to gradual deterioration. The first component undergoes continuous and gradual deterioration, and the second component exhibits an un-fatal, detectable defective state prior to ultimate malfunction. Inspection is equally spaced to reveal the system state, followed by pre-specified preventive maintenance (PM) when: (a) the degradation level of component 1 attains a warning level, or (b) the time elapsed since the defect identification of component 2 reaches the age threshold. Furthermore, opportunistic maintenance (OM) is available for either of these two components when the other one is under PM. The Semi-Markov process is employed for the calculation of system renewal and cost optimization. The effectiveness of the proposed policy is validated via a numerical experiment.

articleTitle: Prediction of Remaining Useful Life Based on SSA-RVM-PF Method for Lithium-ion Battery
abstract: To improve the prediction accuracy of the remaining useful life of lithium-ion battery, a novel SSA-RVM-PF prediction method is proposed. The key prediction mechanism of the proposed method is based on the relevance vector machine (RVM) method. Based on the strong regression ability of RVM, the optimal degradation trajectory of battery capacity can be predicted. Meanwhile, a sparrow search algorithm (SSA) is used to optimize the kernel function parameters of RVM method. Furthermore, a particle filtering (PF) strategy is constructed based on the degradation trajectory, in which the state space model. Simulation results show that the proposed prediction method has the characteristics of high fitting degree of state tracking and high prediction accuracy.

articleTitle: The SBAS Ephemeris Correction and Integrity Parameter Analysis Based on Recursive Least Square Algorithm
abstract: The data processing and quality control of Satellite Based Augmentation System (SBAS) are introduced in detail in this study. The broadcast ephemeris orbit, broadcast clock offset correction and user differential range error (UDRE) parameters are estimated with recursive least square algorithm by using observation data of the 1s sampling rate from 19 stations in China region. The pseudo range residual jump can be weakened when satellite enters and leaves region by applying the quality control algorithm based on fast arrangement sliding window of normal median. Besides the real satellite orbit error and clock offset error are compared with broadcast ephemeris orbit and broadcast clock offset correction, which shows superior performance in consistency. The envelope experiment is conducted based on UDRE, with results aligning with its definition, which meets the integrity requirements. The enhanced single point positioning is conducted by using broadcast ephemeris orbit, clock offset correction and integrity parameters, in which the Klobuchar model is utilized to calculate the ionosphere delay. The result shows that the improvement of 19.3% and 19.5% can be achieved for Horizontal Positioning Error (HPE) and Vertical Positioning Error (VPE), respectively. This study can be used as a reference for the construction and development of SBAS.(Abstract)

articleTitle: Composite Fault Diagnosis of Fighter Based on Wavelet Packet Decomposition and Extreme Gradient Boosting Tree
abstract: This paper studies the diagnosis of composite faults of elevator and pitch angular velocity sensor in F-16 fighter, and proposes a fault diagnosis method based on wavelet packet decomposition and extreme gradient boosting tree (XGBoost). Aiming at the problem that the combined failure of the elevator and pitch angular velocity sensor causes the difference in the time domain of the angle of attack amplitude used for diagnosis to be insignificant, this paper decomposes the angle of attack signal into eight frequency bands through three-layer wavelet packet transform. After decomposition, the energy of each frequency band constitutes a multi-dimensional feature. The high frequency band contains noise and fault information, and its energy distribution can effectively reflect the fault information. Then use the extreme gradient boosting tree to train the fault features to build a multi-classifier. The simulation experiment results verify the effectiveness of the fault diagnosis scheme.

articleTitle: Security Analysis of Distributed Consensus Filtering under Replay Attacks
abstract: In this work, we consider a security problem of consensus-based distributed estimation. Even if without the knowledge of system model, the replay attack can arbitrarily determine a part of sensors to falsify their measurements by repeating the previously recorded sensor readings. It is proven that for a stable system, the estimation error covariance under any given attack strategy not only is bounded, but also can re-enter into the steady state. The Kullback-Leibler (K-L) divergence that describes the detection performance is upper bounded as well, so that the attack is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\epsilon$</tex>-stealthy. On the other hand, when the system is unstable, we prove that the trace of estimation error covariance is lower bounded by an exponential function, which implies that the adversary may severely damage the estimation performance. To guarantee that all of the replay attacks are detectable, we propose a criteria to design the system parameters. Moreover, we analyze the case that the adversary waits to attack until the current measurement is close to the initial part of the recording. Numerical simulations are provided to illustrate the theoretical results in the end.

articleTitle: UAV Fuel Allocation Method Based on Centroid Balance
abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) flight control is a concerned issue. In order to maintain the flight stability, the UAV fuel allocation method based on centroid balance is proposed in this paper. Firstly, the position calculation approach of the center of mass of UAV is given under different pitch angles. Secondly, according to the actual conditions, a model that minimizes the offset of the center of mass is presented. To solve this problem, an approximate local optimal method is proposed. Finally, the method is applied to the situations of level flight and non-level flight, and the results show that the method is effective.

articleTitle: Parallel Commutation Error Compensation Strategy for Sensorless Brushless DC Motor with Asymmetric Back-EMF
abstract: Precise commutation is a significant factor for im-proving the operational efficiency of the brushless DC motor. However, there exists residual error with the motor of three-phase asymmetric back electromotive force (TAEMF) under conventional commutation error correction methods. For solving this problem, a three-parallel channel (TPC) error compensation strategy is proposed. First, the source of error caused by the TAEMF is analyzed. Then, the feedback quantity related to the commutation error is constructed, which is based on the corre-lation between the virtual neutral point relative to the DC-link voltage and the ideal commutation point. Finally, the TPC error correction control system is established by using the feedback quantity, which corrects the error of three commutation signals in three channels. Compared with the conventional methods, the proposed strategy not only compensates the residual error caused by the TAEMF, but also has the advantage of a much simpler circuit configuration. The validity of the proposed strategy has been verified by experimental results.

articleTitle: Prescribed Performance Control of Air-breathing Hypersonic Vehicle with Propulsion System Constraint
abstract: Using prescribed performance control method, a control scheme of a air-breathing hypersonic vehicle (AHV) is designed with the uncertainties of the model and the propulsion system constraint. By prescribed performance, a improved performance function without the initial condition information is designed to transfer error constraint into stable control problem. In order to ensure the propulsion system work condition, the status of AHV must be restricted in a certain range. So the AHV control system with scramjet condition constraint is development by adaptive and prescribed performance control method. The uncertainties of AHV model are introduced to the control system. Finally, the performance of the designed AHV control system is achieved by several simulation results.

articleTitle: Adaptive fault-tolerant control of air-breathing hypersonic vehicles with variable geometry inlet
abstract: A novel adaptive fault-tolerant controller is proposed for a switched model of air-breathing hypersonic vehicle with variable geometry inlet (AHV-VGI). The VGI with movable translation fairing is used to capture sufficient air mass flow of scramjet to provide sufficient thrust. A switched model is firstly established with respect to different flight envelop, and the actuator fault and backlash nonlinearity are considered. In order to avoid the control discontinuity or oscillation caused by the sudden change of switching signal. An adaptive fault-tolerant controller based on barrier Lyapunov function is then designed to steer velocity and altitude tracking errors into predefined arbitrarily small residual sets, wherein the effects of actuator fault and backlash nonlinearity are compensated successfully by estimating their upper bounds. Different from other existing switching control strategies, the proposed controller does not contain switching information. Simulations on the switched model are carried out to prove the effectiveness of the designed controller.

articleTitle: Intermediate Observer based Fault-Tolerant Control for Fuzzy Stochastic Systems with Actuator Fault
abstract: This paper discusses the fault estimation and fault-tolerant control of fuzzy stochastic systems under disturbance. Firstly, an intermediate observer is devised to reconstruct the state and actuator fault. The difference from the classical intermediate observer is that this method introduces the output estimation error feedback into the observer design, so this method expands the design freedom. Then a fault-tolerant controller based on the information estimated by the observer is designed. Lastly, a simulation of cart model is provided to show the reliability of our method.

articleTitle: A Deep Learning Method based on SRN-YOLO for Forest Fire Detection
abstract: Sensor-based methods and vision-based methods with manual features selection have been widely used in forest fire detection. However, they have limited detection areas and are only effective in some specific scenarios. In this paper, SRN-YOLO, an improved version of YOLOv3, is proposed to reach a higher accuracy and lightweight network structure for forest fire detection. First, a sparse residual network (SRN) is proposed, which solves the potential overfitting problem by modifying the skip-connection to the sparse-connection. Then, based on the sparse-connection, the residual units in the classic YOLOv3 are replaced by the sparse residual modules, and the backbone network Darknet-53 is improved to obtain the proposed SRN-YOLO network. Through comparison experiments with other YOLO-based networks such as YOLO-LITE and Tinier-YOLO, the results show that the proposed network in this paper is effective and lightweight, and can achieve higher accuracy for forest fire detection.

articleTitle: Tightly Coupled GNSS, INS and Visual Odometry for Accurate and Robust Vehicle Positioning
abstract: High-precise vehicle positioning in urban environment is very crucial for modern transportation system. However, the traditional GNSS positioning cannot fully meet the requirement under complex environment. Thus, multi-sensor integrated navigation is inevitable. In this paper, a tightly coupled data fusion system of GNSS, INS and Visual Odometry is proposed to achieve accurate and robust vehicle positioning. The error state Extended Kalman Filter is employed for the multi-sensor integration. In order to make the most use of GNSS information, both pseduorange and carrier phase measurements are tightly coupled via the double-differenced RTK model. The Multi-State Constraint Kalman Filter is adopted to further integrate the stereo visual odometry. The proposed integration system is evaluated by field experiments in complex urban environment. The results show that the GNSS/INS/VO integrated navigation system provides more accurate and continuous positioning results than GNSS alone in GNSS-challenged environment.

articleTitle: Performance of PPN Guided Missile with Arbitrary Time-Varying Speed against Stationary Targets: New Findings
abstract: The performance of the pure proportional navigation (PPN) guidance law against the stationary target is restudied, when the missile speed is arbitrarily time-varying. Based on the classical differential geometry theory, the analytical solutions of the line-of-sight (LOS) angle, LOS rate, missile lead angle, and closing speed of PPN are derived in the missile's arc-length domain. The capture condition of PPN against the stationary target is thoroughly analyzed, when the guided missile is with arbitrary-time-varying-speed. Some new theoretical findings are presented, such as the maximum relative range, maximum trajectory curvature, curvature integral, and missile flying range.

articleTitle: GAN-SLAM: GAN based Monocular Visual-Inertial Simultaneous Localization and Mapping in Dark Environments
abstract: In recent years, visual-inertial Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) techniques have achieved excellent results due to the complementary nature of visual and inertial sensors, the challenges remain in some environments. When encountering a challenging environment, image features become an important factor affecting the success rate and accuracy of localization of SLAM system. Due to the Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) has the advantage of extracting effective features more accurately, this paper makes a new attempt to replace traditional features with those generated by the network. We combine the state-of-the-art CNN of optical flow estimation and iterative optimization model of traditional SLAM framework, which achieves the accuracy and robustness in challenging environments. To show the performance of our method, some state-of-the-art visual-inertial methods are tested and compared with the challenging sequences of public dataset. Experimental results show that the proposed method can achieve better results in accuracy and robustness and works reliably well for challenging environments.

articleTitle: A Multisensor-based Tightly Coupled Integrated Navigation System
abstract: We present a tightly coupled multi-sensor integrated navigation and localization system based on graph optimization. To be specific, we calculate the preintegrated IMU factor by retraction strategy and use the reprojection error of the stereo camera as the visual landmark factor. Then we demonstrate their fusion with 3D line and plane primitives in the Lidar point cloud in a graph-based optimization framework. Furthermore, a segmented optimization algorithm is designed in the system and the widely used GPS and closure loop are added as constraints. The resulting visual-inertial-Lidar-GPS fusion navigation system is validated on a real-world dataset.

articleTitle: M2-Conformer: Multi-modal CNN- Transformer for Driving Behavior Detection
abstract: As playing a key role in the development of Advanced Driver Assistance System (ADAS), driving behavior detection has attracted more and more attention over recent years. In this paper, a novel hybrid deep learning framework, Multi-Modal CNN-Transformer (M2-Conformer) is proposed for driving behavior detection from video frames and multivariate vehicle signals. The M2-Conformer is constructed with both Transformer and CNN architecture in paralleled branch to extract driving scene features and vehicle dynamics features respectively. Specially, a dynamic token sparsification is utilized for Transformer branch to prune redundant tokens hierarchically, which makes the framework easy to obtain speed-up. To enhance the performance, a custom-built Feature Aggregation Module (FAM) is designed for M2-Conformer to generate aggregated features from different branches with higher-quality. Experiments carried out on a naturalistic driving data set indicate that the proposed M2-Conformer achieves a superior complexity/accuracy trade-off for driving behavior detection compared to other state-of-the-art architectures.

articleTitle: A Bioinspired Polarization Sensor/Sun Tracker/IMU Integrated System for Attitude Determination in GNSS-Challenged Environments
abstract: Determining attitudes in Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS)-challenged environments is a key issue. This paper designs a bionic integrated navigation system for attitude determination by integrating a polarization sensor, a sun tracker and an inertial measurement unit (IMU). To improve the robustness of heading estimation, a multi-mode automatic switching algorithm based on threshold values and polarization angle mismatch error is proposed. A self-calibration algorithm for sensor installation errors has also been developed to improve the heading accuracy. Compared with the existing researches, the system proposed in this paper integrates the sun tracker and the polarization sensor for the first time, which could realize continuous attitude estimation during the daytime. To validate the effectiveness of the proposed automatic switching algorithm, a semi-simulation static test was carried out. The results show that the proposed automatic switching algorithm for the integrated system has the best heading estimation performance compared with other methods in terms of robustness and stability.

articleTitle: Projection Operator-Based Fault-Tolerant Backstepping Adaptive Control of Fixed-Wing UAV Against Actuator Faults
abstract: Aiming at solving the problem of the loss of actuator effectiveness, a fault-tolerant backstepping control method for fixed-wing unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) is proposed in this paper. Firstly, the attitude dynamic model of fixed-wing UAV and the actuator fault model are introduced. Secondly, based on projection operator, adaptive law is considered to estimate the bounded control effectiveness. Then, by using Lyapunov stability analysis, the fixed-wing UAV is able to track the expected targets even when the actuator becomes faulty. Finally, the effectiveness of the designed controller is verified by simulation results.

articleTitle: Right Invariant SE2 (3) - EKF for Relative Navigation in Learning-based Visual Inertial Odometry
abstract: The visual inertial odometry(VIO) has shown great potential localization ability in robots' autonomy tasks. Although the learning-based VIO method shows promising results as it is robust to different lighting conditions without sensors calibration. It is not necessary to learn the kinematics of IMU as its model is well studied. In this work, we propose a learning based VIO framework which uses a right invariant SE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> (3)-EKF to combine the measurements from IMU and relative poses from learning-based visual odometry. The novel SE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> (3) - EKF defines the right invariant error of the relative navigation model on matrix Lie group and derives the associated error state differential equations. As the relative pose of the learning-based VO is compatible with the right invariant error, the consistence issue of tradition EKF is overcame. The experiments on the KITTI datasets have shown the superior performance of the proposed method compared to the other learning-based methods.

articleTitle: Research on UAV autonomous deformation strategy based on deep learning
abstract: To improve the autonomous deformation capability of morphing aircraft, a new method was proposed, which established an autonomous deformation strategy knowledge base based on deep learning. A longitudinal nonlinear dynamic model of variable-sweep-wing unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) was obtained by using multi-rigid-body modeling. DATCOM was used to perform aerodynamic analysis, and then aerodynamic coefficient fitting formula was calculated. Based on prior knowledge, a deformation strategy was designed, which could generate training data for deep learning. A deep neural network (DNN), so-called autonomous deformation strategy knowledge base, was trained by using these data, which could output optimal sweep angle according to current flight states and flight mission.
